name: Araiyakushi-Mae
tagline: Shinjuku in 17 minutes and Shibuya in 27 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000.
summary: The station is in Nakano City, where Seibu run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 27 minutes to Otemachi, 17 minutes to Shinjuku, 27 minutes to Shibuya and 47 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. The station stands 37.2 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 9.4 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 37.2 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 29.1 m to 38.5 m, a difference of 9.4 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of less than 0.5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 4 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 0.5 to 3 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 16 clinics and 12 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 徳静会横畠外科胃腸科病院, about 11 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 健友会中野共立病院, about 15 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Seibu Shinjuku Line.
congestion: Seibu Shinjuku Line runs at 148% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 下落合→高田馬場, which this station is not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥80,000 to ¥90,000 and 1K ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. 1LDK ¥150,000 to ¥160,000 and 2LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the low side. What holds the figure down: only one line, the {line}, serving the station. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For safety, Numabukuro; for the number of medical facilities, Araiyakushi-Mae.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Araiyakushi-Mae. It is served by the same lines as Araiyakushi-Mae. Journey times to the main business districts are much the same. On how easy the shopping is, Araiyakushi-Mae comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: For rail connections, Nakano; for safety, Araiyakushi-Mae.
neighbours.note: About 1.5 km from Araiyakushi-Mae in a straight line. Nakano also has the JR Chuo Rapid Line, JR Chuo-Sobu Line (Local) and Tokyo Metro Tozai Line, which Araiyakushi-Mae does not. With more lines, Nakano is the better connected of the two. To Tokyo, for instance, Nakano is 12 minutes quicker. On safety, though, Araiyakushi-Mae comes out ahead.

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 12 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Seibu Shinjuku Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
